You use the zero conditional to talk about real situations and facts.
If we want to continue working as programmers, we need to get used to everyday changes.
If you don't have the knowledge and tools to do it, it's difficult to create an entire system with millions of lines of code.

You use this conditional to explain two situations that complement each other and that are always real. The first part explains a condition. The second explains the result, consequence or direct relation to the first condition.

Both parts need to be in present simple and they are always about true situations that are obvious, rules or general situations which always have the same result.

For zero conditional, this is the structure you use:
If / When + sentence in present simple tense (condition), + sentence in simple present (result).


For example:
If you use HTML, you can design a website.

Notice that the clauses are separated by a comma when the first clause is the condition.
Simple Present Tense, Present Continuous, and Be Going to Review to Talk About Future Trends in a Specific Topic
In English, there are several ways to talk about the future. We can talk about the future using present simple, present continuous and be going to. Let's see how that works.
It talks about the changes that software is having in the next years.
It's not going to be necessary for people to go to the doctor for medical assistance.
I am presenting an article next month.

Simple present

Normally, you use the present simple to refer to routines, daily events, and things that usually happen or actions that you frequently do, but you can also talk about the future; you can use the present simple when you talk about something planned in advance:

Follow this structure to talk in present simple:
Subject + verb in present + complement.


Examples:
We work with HTML 5.0 until they release the new version.
Software creating starts next month.

Present continuous

You use the present continuous to say that an action is happening at the same moment of speaking or that an action is temporarily happening in the present. However, you can also use this tense to talk about plans in the future.

This structure is the one you follow to form the present continuous:
Subject + be (are - is - am) + verb + ing + complement.


Examples:
We are designing the website for that company next month.
They are planning on using our software on their next project.

Be going to

You use the structure be going to to talk about plans in the future. You can use going to when you are sure something happening because there is evidence or plans about it.

We use this structure to talk with going to:
Subject + be (are-is-am) + going to + verb + complement.


Examples:
I'm going to work with requirement elicitations.
They are going to observe the company to learn about our workflow.

contents.content: Let's talk about software in the future…
Instructions: Complete the following steps. Fill in the Self-Assessment.

images.text:
Jacob: Hi, what are you reading?
Paul: I'm reading an article about software. It talks about the changes that software is having in the next years.
You know the world of tech moves so fast. So they are analyzing some trends to show projections for the future. It says that smartphones are going to do everything. At the moment, they're doing many things. People make transactions, they buy things, and they even study in their phones. But I'm sure there are going to be more advanced applications. For example, in the future, it's not going to be necessary for people to go to the doctor for medical assistance, because through different applications they can have a checkup.

Jacob: But how does software change?
Paul: Software has modifications every day. For instance, smartphones are products that can easily change in order to adapt to an environment. Some studies mention that software may change for a variety of reasons and there are important advantages for programmers and users when this happens. For example, they can add new features, also they can correct faults and they can restructure codes to accommodate future variations. So we have to learn how to do all those software modifications. .

Jacob: Yes, that's absolutely true. If we want to continue working as programmers, we need to get used to everyday changes, right? I am presenting an article next month about the new educational needs due to those probable changes. I think all professors are wondering the same; if they just teach how to write software, we don't learn how to write real code. When you start programming, you realize how hard it is to juggle all of those numbers. It's difficult to create an entire system with millions of lines of code if you don't have the knowledge and tools to do it.
